title: AI attribution: configure-only, or configure plus an enforcing backstop?
context: Claude Code and Aider expose PROJECT-level knobs paqad can write at onboarding. Codex and Cursor only expose USER-level config under the developer's home directory, which onboarding should not write. So a config-only fix is provably incomplete across providers. A commit-time/delivery-time backstop that detects known AI attribution trailers works for every provider including ones with no knob at all.

options.label: Configure what we can, plus a delivery-time backstop that catches the rest
Configure only (write the knobs we can, report honestly on the rest)

rationale: Config alone is provably incomplete (Codex and Cursor are user-level only), so the promise needs a delivery-time backstop to be true on every provider.
